title: Collaboration: Expire Presence Without Disconnecting Other Tabs
businessContext: Closing one browser tab marks a user offline despite another active tab. Delayed heartbeats also resurrect disconnected sessions.
problemStatement: Implement solution({ now, sessions }). now is a nonnegative safe integer. Each valid snapshot has nonempty id/userId, nonnegative safe-integer version and expiresAt, and boolean online. Snapshots may arrive out of order. For each session id retain the highest version; equal-version first arrival wins. All versions of one session id belong to the same user. A retained session is active iff online and expiresAt > now. Return { onlineUsers, activeSessions }, where onlineUsers contains unique user IDs in ascending JavaScript string order. Empty sessions gives empty users and zero active sessions.
constraints: Implement the synchronous solution(input) contract exactly. Do not mutate input; all inputs are JSON data.
This is a deterministic state model. It does not open sockets, send notifications, authorize real users, or establish media connections.
candidateTasks: Reproduce the starter failure, implement the invariant, and pass every authored case.
How would you implement leases, typing-indicator expiry, and disconnect tombstone retention across presence servers?

testCases.name: Aggregate multiple tabs once per user
One closed tab does not close another
First equal version wins and output is sorted

hints: Write down validation and replay precedence before changing state.
Use stable IDs and monotonic sequence/version values; preserve input ownership.
alternativeApproaches: Use an append-only event log with transactional projections.
Use a database snapshot plus a versioned resume cursor.
commonMistakes: Trusting delivery order or treating retries as new operations.
Mutating caller-owned arrays or accepting cross-channel data.
Presenting a fixture result as a guarantee of real-time delivery or media connectivity.
